# Florida Fast Title

**What this is:** the third-party title company that transfers every manufactured-home title Parakeet touches and schedules every abandoned-home auction — single-sourced, with no alternative anywhere in the process library.

**Status:** current — 2026-08-30

## The facts
- **What they supply:** title transfer, VIN investigation and abandoned-home auction scheduling. Referred to throughout the library as **FFT**.
- **Three processes run through them, and only through them:** every **POH sale title transfer** (SOP 005), the **post-eviction title package and auction** (the unnumbered post-eviction title SOP), and the **resident turn-in** path where a resident hands the home back voluntarily.
- **Who uses it:** the Title Department / Evictions send the packages; the Community Manager supplies the closing documents, resident ID and home identifiers, with the Regional Manager copied; the buyer or bidder signs. Title updates the **Asset Transfer tab in Rent Manager** with every transfer detail and uploads the received title to the resident profile and the Assets tab.
- **Title transfer takes approximately 7 to 10 business days.** FFT updates its customer portal once documents are received. Packages go **overnight mail** in both directions, with FFT sending the finished title back on an overnight label Parakeet supplies.
- **The POH sale package:** Cover Sheet, Title, **3 Powers of Attorney signed in blue ink**, and a copy of the buyer's ID — a state driver's licence or ID card with photo, or a US passport with proof of valid visa. Nothing else is acceptable.
- **The post-eviction package:** Cover Sheet, Landlord Questionnaire, Writ of Possession, Authorization Letter — emailed to FFT and logged in the Rent Manager Eviction Workflow History/Notes.
- **VIN investigation:** where a home has no VIN, **FFT investigates or works with the DMV to have a new VIN processed** before the auction can be scheduled. The Community Manager supplies whatever is found — VIN / HUD number / decal / tag number, year, make and model, length, width, colour.
- **The abandonment clock: FFT mails the Letter of Abandonment to all owners, granting approximately 21 days (timing varies) to reclaim the home.** Reclaiming requires **certified funds** covering rent, late fees, legal fees and FFT's own charges.
- FFT schedules the auction and emails Evictions, who forwards to the Community and Regional Manager and creates a calendar invite. **The Community Manager signs no documents at an FFT auction.** If a bidder attends, the highest bidder pays the awarded bid price including home cost, tax and tag/title fee, signs 3 POAs and provides acceptable ID. **No bidder → FFT proceeds to obtain title, and Parakeet purchases the home for $1.**
- Title timing after mailing is **approximately 30 days; 5 to 7 months if the case is in declaratory judgment** (SOP 107).
- **How critical: high and single-sourced.** No alternative title vendor appears anywhere in 242 process files. Losing FFT would stop every POH sale from completing, every post-eviction recovery, and every abandoned-home auction — and the company has no in-house title function to fall back on; the desk that handles it is called five different things across six documents and is defined nowhere.
- **The lien exception: where a lien exists on the home, the auction goes to Vector Law instead** (SOP 107 step 34b). FFT handles the no-lien path only — and neither title SOP mentions liens or Vector Law at all, so the liened-home title path is documented nowhere.
- **Known problems:** FFT is **Florida-only in a five-state portfolio.** There is no GA, SC, NC or MA title process anywhere in the library — while SOP 822 documents a South Carolina statutory 20-day abandoned-home auction under SC Code 29-15-10 that appears in neither title SOP, and SOP 812 states Georgia has no park-specific title shortcut and routes abandoned homes to Legal, a path with no SOP behind it.
- Further problems: the 7–10 day estimate is **a vendor estimate with no internal deadline, no escalation path and no tracking artifact** beyond the Asset Transfer tab; the reclaim window does not reconcile (FFT's ~21 days vs SC's statutory 20 days vs no window at all in SOP 107); and both title SOPs are unnumbered PDFs with no owner, version or effective date.
